idea: A working boat's hull: thick white paint laid on by hand every spring, a red waterline, and rust running down from every fitting.
world: A small fishing boat on a slipway in a cold harbour. Nobody designs it; it gets painted because the sea eats it. The topsides are chalk white because white paint is cheap and shows the rot; below the waterline is antifouling, a dull oxide red; the boot-top between them is one clean red stripe cut with masking tape, the only careful thing on the boat. Every iron fitting bleeds rust straight down. Salt dulls everything.

signature.says: The waterline. One red band of even width runs round the whole car at the hull's lowest clean line, the skirt's crease, where water would sit. Above it everything is chalk white; below it everything is dull oxide red, the antifouling. It starts where the nose first meets the water, follows the car's own lowest crease along both flanks and across the tail, and ends only where the hull ends. It never climbs a panel and never bends for a shape: water finds its level.

dna.says: Everything is put on by a brush or runs down by gravity. Bands are level and of one width along their whole length, their edges hard as a masked line. Rust is a streak: it starts at a point (a fastener, a seam's end, a hinge) and runs straight down the surface, 2 to 4 times longer than it is wide, widest at its source, fading at its tail; several from one row of fittings run parallel, never joining. Shapes are bands, dots and streaks; nothing is drawn as an outline, nothing curves of its own accord. Widths: the waterline 4 cm; a repaint patch 20 to 40 cm; a rust streak 0.6 to 1.2 cm wide; a fitting 1 to 2 cm across. Rhythm: fittings sit in rows along the car's own seams, at a hand's uneven spacing.

colours.name: Chalk white
colours.job: the topsides: everything above the waterline, warm and dry

colours.name: Antifouling
colours.job: everything below the waterline: dull, heavy, the colour of old brick

colours.name: Boot-top red
colours.job: the waterline only: the one bright, careful thing

colours.name: Rust
colours.job: streaks from the fittings, and a bloom round each

colours.name: Tar black
colours.job: iron: the fittings, the inner car, the tyres, the openings

meet: White and antifouling never touch: the boot-top red always lies between them, one hard masked edge on each side. Rust lies over white or over antifouling, soft at its tail. Tar black meets the rest only where a fitting or an opening is.

surfaces.job: the topsides: bone-dry, flatter than matte, the brush left in it
the antifouling: dead flat, soft underfoot
the boot-top: enamel, the only shine on the hull
the streaks and blooms from every fitting
the inner car's iron, tarred: rough and dark
the tyres: old fenders, greyed by salt

ageing: Painted last spring, a season at sea since. The white has gone chalky and shows the brush; it's whiter where a patch was redone. The antifouling has a patch one shade off where it was touched up on the slipway. Rust runs from every iron fitting, longest where the water drains. No chips, no scratches, no dirt: salt and rust are the only wear, and they come from the fittings, never from nowhere.

large.what: the hull in two halves, white over oxide red, split by the level red waterline round the whole car

fullness: Mostly empty: big flat white and big flat red, the waterline between. The detail is rust, and rust only lives where there's iron: a dozen streaks on the whole car, a few blooms, one patch. Nothing is added to fill a space.
never: A line that isn't the car's own or the waterline
Anchors, ropes, flags, fish or any nautical picture
Rust that doesn't start at a fitting or a seam
A stripe, a shape or a sticker for decoration
